title: Directory replication rights exercised by a non-DC principal

alert.rule_name: Credential Access: Directory Replication Rights Exercised by Non-DC Principal
alert.description: A security principal that is not a domain controller invoked the directory replication service (DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges) against the domain naming context. Replication rights allow an account to request the password hash of any principal in the domain, including krbtgt, without ever touching a domain controller's disk or memory.
alert.detection_logic: Security EventID=4662 WHERE ObjectType = '{19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}' (domainDNS) AND Properties CONTAINS ANY ('{1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}' /* DS-Replication-Get-Changes */, '{1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}' /* DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All */) AND SubjectUserName NOT IN (domain_controller_computer_accounts) AND SubjectUserName NOT IN (approved_replication_service_accounts)

replication_guids.{1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}: DS-Replication-Get-Changes — the extended right permitting a principal to request replicated directory data.
replication_guids.{1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}: DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All — extends the above to secret attributes, i.e. password hashes (unicodePwd, ntPwdHistory, supplementalCredentials).
replication_guids.{19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}: ObjectType domainDNS — the domain naming context itself, the root object replication is requested against.

access_mask_decode.0x100: ACTRL_DS_CONTROL_ACCESS — exercise of an extended right, not a normal read or write.

enrichment.principal_role: THESHIRE\pgustavo is an interactive domain user account. It is not a domain controller computer account and not a directory-synchronisation service account. In a healthy domain, the only principals invoking DsGetNCChanges are DC computer accounts replicating with each other, and any explicitly delegated sync accounts (for example Azure AD Connect).
enrichment.network_path: The two connections from WORKSTATION5 to 172.18.38.5 immediately precede the alert: TCP/135 is the RPC endpoint mapper, and TCP/49674 is the dynamically-assigned port the endpoint mapper hands back for the drsuapi interface. This is the wire footprint of a remote DRSUAPI bind.
enrichment.source_binary: The connections originate from C:\Users\pgustavo\Desktop\GruntHTTP.exe — an unsigned executable running from a user desktop directory, not from a system or program-files path.
enrichment.logon_correlation: Security/4624 logon ID 0x824909 (network logon, Kerberos, from 172.18.39.5) is the same logon ID recorded on all three 4662 records, tying the replication request back to the WORKSTATION5 session.
enrichment.blast_radius: A successful replication of the domain naming context should be treated as full domain credential compromise, including the krbtgt account. krbtgt compromise enables forged Kerberos ticket-granting tickets, which survive password resets of individual users.

verdict.rationale: A user-context executable on WKS-4471 connected to DC01 over RPC and the correlated Kerberos network logon exercised both replication extended rights against the domain object. This is a DCSync-like, potentially domain-compromising sequence, but the supplied telemetry also shows highly privileged group membership and provides no customer authorization context or proof that secret data was returned. An evidence-bounded SOC analyst should urgently escalate rather than autonomously contain.

acceptable_alternatives.rationale: Malicious is fully equivalent because O1 (R000079, R000080) shows a user-Desktop executable initiating the RPC sequence and O3 (R000142, R000143, R000144) records both replication extended rights against the domain object. O4 (R000136) establishes privileged group membership but cannot resolve authorization or negate the DCSync-like tradecraft; escalation remains required.

observations.desc: Sysmon recorded C:\Users\j.marsh\Desktop\svcupdate.exe PID 2064 initiating TCP connections from 10.24.8.21 to DC01 at 10.24.8.10 on ports 135 and 49674.
DC01 recorded a successful Kerberos network logon for CORP\j.marsh from 10.24.8.21 source port 59696 with logon ID 0x824909 and an elevated token.
event_refs: Security EventID 4624 on DC01, logon ID 0x824909, source 10.24.8.21:59696

observations.desc: DC01 recorded three successful Security 4662 Control Access events for CORP\j.marsh under logon ID 0x824909 and ObjectType {19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9}; two include property {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2} and one includes {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}.
event_refs: Security EventID 4662 on DC01, logon ID 0x824909, Properties {1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}
Security EventID 4662 on DC01, logon ID 0x824909, Properties {1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2}

observations.desc: Security 4627 for logon ID 0x824909 lists CORP\j.marsh with domain group SIDs ending in 512, 518, and 519, SID S-1-5-32-544, and integrity SID S-1-16-12288.
event_refs: Security EventID 4627 on DC01, logon ID 0x824909

inferences.desc: The port-135 connection followed by a connection to port 49674 on the DC is consistent with RPC endpoint mapping followed by communication with a dynamically assigned RPC service.

The 4662 property GUIDs correspond to DS-Replication-Get-Changes and DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All on the domain object, so the correlated sequence is consistent with DCSync-style directory replication access.

The observed group SIDs indicate that j.marsh held powerful directory privileges in this session, making legitimate administrative replication possible but not establishing that this specific activity was authorized.
If secret-bearing directory attributes were returned, the potential impact includes broad domain credential exposure; successful hash or secret extraction is not shown by the provided events.

investigations.desc: Confirm with the customer whether CORP\j.marsh was authorized to perform directory replication at this time and obtain the relevant change, backup, migration, or test record.
Collect and analyze svcupdate.exe, including file hash, signature state, provenance, execution lineage, and endpoint-detection telemetry.
Review packet, directory-service, and endpoint telemetry to determine the RPC interface and whether replicated secret attributes were actually returned.
Investigate how j.marsh obtained its privileged memberships and review recent changes to replication rights, privileged groups, and account credentials.
Hunt for additional replication-rights events, anomalous Kerberos activity, credential use, and lateral movement associated with j.marsh or WKS-4471.

unknowns.desc: Customer authorization and the approved operational purpose, if any, for this replication activity are unknown.
The signature state, trust, provenance, and intended function of svcupdate.exe are unknown from the provided telemetry.
Whether password hashes or other secret attributes were successfully returned, stored, or used is not observed in the provided window/chain.
